details.label: Summary
details.text: Several clusters of strong to occasionally severe storms may gradually move into a more unstable air mass this evening. Some potential for MCS development and a subsequent severe wind gust risk is evident. Confidence is low, but a Watch is possible

details.label: Discussion
details.text: As of 0100 UTC, regional radar imagery showed several clusters of strong to occasional severe storms ongoing from southern WY, across eastern CO into southwestern KS. Driven in part by a broad post-frontal upslope flow regime, convective coverage has steadily increased this evening. With numerous storms ongoing, some cold pool amalgamation has been noted. Recent CAM guidance shows this continuing with a potentially more organized cluster or MCS evolving later this evening. The air mass to the north of the front is still relatively warm and moist which is supporting moderate buoyancy (MLCAPE 1500-2500 J/kg). Deep-layer shear is more modest between 25-35 kt, but slightly elongated mid and upper-level hodographs are supportive of some organization of multicells and clusters. Overall shear profiles are also expected to increase later this evening with the nocturnal low-level jet. The primary uncertainty remains the storm-scale organization of the cold pool and how that may influence the severe risk. With the environment more than supportive of strong updrafts and current storm maintenance, further clustering and eventual organization is possible, especially where low-level convergence is maximized along and north of the front. Given this potential, some severe risk could evolve later this evening and overnight. The need for a watch is very uncertain, but conditions will be monitored
